Anchor.description:
Machine-checkable location behind an evidence item, pinned to a commit so it can be
rechecked later (`claims-mcp recheck`).

Rust note: serde's default enum form is "externally tagged": `{"file": {...}}` or
`{"search": {...}}`, like a one-key dict whose key names the variant.

oneOf.description: A file or line range.
A search; with zero hits, a demonstrated absence.

Claim.description: A single atomic, falsifiable assertion and everything recorded about it.

artifacts.description: Artifacts the claim is about (paths, modules, URLs).

derived_from.description: Parent claims this one refines (upstream trace links).

kind.description: What sort of property it asserts.

seal.description: Integrity seal over the claim's own fields, its evidence ids, and its latest verdict.

source.description: Where the claim came from (prompt, spec section, ticket).

source_anchor.description: Commit-pinned location of the text that makes the claim, such as a README line.

updated_at.description: When the claim last changed in any way.

verdicts.description: Append-only verdict history; the last entry is current.

ClaimKind.description: What sort of property a claim asserts.

oneOf.description: Observable behavior or output.
Quality attribute such as usability or maintainability.
Contract with another component, API, or user.
Latency, throughput, or resource bound.
Protection against harm to people or property.
Confidentiality, integrity, or availability property.
Statement about documentation content.
Imposed limitation such as a language, license, or dependency rule.

ClaimLevel.description: Position of a claim in the requirements hierarchy, from broadest to narrowest.

oneOf.description: Whole-system requirement or top-level task instruction.
Software-level requirement.
Requirement on one component or module.
Requirement on one function or type.
Assertion about a concrete produced artifact.

ClaimStatus.description:
Lifecycle state of a claim. Claims are retired instead of deleted.

Rust note: `tag = "state"` writes the variant name into a `state` field, giving
`{"state":"active"}` or `{"state":"retired","reason":...,"retired_at":...}`.

oneOf.description: The claim is in force.
The claim was withdrawn; it stays in the file so trace links remain valid.

Evidence.description: One piece of evidence attached to a claim.

anchor.description: Commit-pinned location that `recheck` can verify; absent for free-text-only evidence.

locator.description: Where to find it: `path:line`, test name, command, or URL.

seal.description: Integrity seal; absent only in an unsealed catalog or after tampering.

stance.description: Whether it supports or refutes the claim.

EvidenceKind.description: The form a piece of evidence takes.

oneOf.description: Result of an executed test.
Observation from reading an artifact.
Result of reasoning or static analysis.
Observation from running the system.
Proof artifact or proof-checker output.
Captured log or command output.
Anything else.

FileAnchor.description: A file, or lines in it, at the commit that was checked out when the anchor was recorded.

commit.description: Full commit id of `HEAD` when the anchor was recorded.

dirty.description: `true` if the file had uncommitted changes then, so `commit` may not show what was seen.

lines.description: The anchored lines; the whole file when absent.

path.description: Path relative to the repository root.

LineRange.description: An inclusive, 1-based range of lines in a file.

Seal.description:
Integrity seal on a catalog record: an HMAC over the record's content and its position in
the catalog (see `src/seal.rs`). The origin is covered by the MAC, so relabeling an adopted
record as server-sealed invalidates it.

oneOf.description: The server sealed the record when a tool created or changed it.
`claims-mcp seal --adopt` sealed a record that had no seal (catalog migration).

SearchAnchor.description:
A `git grep -E` search and how many lines it matched at the pinned commit. With zero hits
it shows that something does not exist, such as a feature a document promises.

case_insensitive.description: Whether the search ignores case (`git grep -i`).

commit.description: Full commit id of `HEAD` when the search was recorded.

dirty.description: `true` if a scope path had uncommitted changes then.

hits.description: Matching lines at `commit`, counted by the server.

pattern.description: POSIX extended regular expression, as `git grep -E` reads it.

scope.description: Paths searched, relative to the repository root (`.` is the whole repository).

Stance.description: Whether a piece of evidence supports or refutes its claim (FEVER terminology).

oneOf.description: The evidence shows the claim holds.
The evidence shows the claim does not hold.
The evidence is relevant but decides nothing.

Verdict.description: A FEVER verdict an auditor can record.

oneOf.description: Cited evidence shows the claim holds.
Cited evidence shows the claim does not hold.
The available evidence cannot decide the claim.

VerdictRecord.description: One entry in a claim's append-only verdict history.

auditor.description: Who or what recorded it (a person or a model id).

evidence_ids.description: Evidence on the same claim that the verdict relies on.

seal.description: Integrity seal; also chains to the previous verdict's seal.

VerificationMethod.description: How a claim is meant to be verified (IEEE 1012 / INCOSE methods plus formal proof).

oneOf.description: Reading code, documents, or output.
Reasoning, calculation, or static analysis.
Running the system and observing behavior without instrumentation.
Executing a defined test with pass/fail criteria.
Machine-checked or rigorous mathematical proof.

description:
The whole catalog document.

Claims are kept sorted by id; because ids only grow, appending preserves the order and
lookups are a binary search (O(log n)).

next_claim_seq_seal.description:
Integrity seal over `schema_version` and `next_claim_seq` (see `src/seal.rs`). Each
counter has its own seal, next to it, so branches that advanced different counters
merge without touching each other's seal.

next_evidence_seq.description: Next never-used, catalog-wide evidence sequence number.

schema_version.description: Catalog format version described by this schema.
